description:
FILED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  PRE-EXISTING.

perl-tests/method.t has a row named exactly "DESTROY without a leading sub is
legal and gets called"; perl produces it, PCL does not produce it at all.
perl-tests/ref.t:307 uses the same spelling:

    DESTROY {
        return unless $string;
        main::is ($string, 'good');
        main::isnt (ref shift, 'HASH');
    }

perl parses a bare `NAME BLOCK` at statement level as a sub definition for the
handful of names that take it (DESTROY, BEGIN-like slots); PCL does not, so
the method is never installed.

Note the OTHER half of the same rows: even when DESTROY IS defined with `sub`,
PCL never fires it (docs/not-supported.md '`DESTROY` called by garbage
collector'), so ref.t's rows at lines 310/313/440 are missing for that reason
whichever spelling is used -- probed with a `sub DESTROY` reproducer, perl
prints "DESTROY fired", PCL prints nothing.  Fixing this task alone recovers
nothing there; it is method.t's one row and the correctness of the parse.
subject: `DESTROY { ... }` written WITHOUT a leading `sub` is legal perl and is not installed as a method by PCL
